page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a total of 1123 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor featuring 112 physical cores, 224 vCPUs with hyper-threading, and a base clock speed of 2.1 GHz. It includes 2952.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 13.18 GB of RAM per core. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be handled via network-attached options.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The memory subsystem demonstrates exceptional throughput, achieving top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 13946.39 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth of 188.23 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories, respectively. In database and network workloads, the server achieves top-tier results, including 221.56 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 209.03 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

This server is designed for massive parallel processing tasks, including large-scale machine learning, LLM training, and complex scientific simulations. The inclusion of eight high-capacity H200 GPUs makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads that can fully saturate its massive GPU memory and parallel processing capabilities, though the lack of local SSD storage requires careful architectural planning for data-intensive pipelines. It is highly suited for deep learning, large-scale AI inference, and high-performance computing applications.
